title: Add pricing summary section with comparison and Most Popular badge
description:
Add compact pricing summary between portfolio and testimonials.

Requirements:
- Compact version of the 3 tiers (title, price range, one-liner each)
- "Most Popular" badge on middle tier
- "See Full Pricing" link → /pricing
- Keep distinct from the services section above (use different layout or visual style)
- Use azimuth-ui Card, Text components

Psychology: repetition reinforces message, framing (investment language).

title: Add portfolio/work samples section with placeholder content
description:
Add portfolio section to landing page.

Requirements:
- Grid of project cards (thumbnail placeholder, title, one-line result)
- Current pilot website as first entry
- Placeholder cards for future work
- "View All Work" link → /portfolio
- Empty state styling for placeholder cards (subtle "Coming soon" overlay)
- Use azimuth-ui Card, Text components

Psychology: social proof (real work builds trust), anticipatory for future projects.

title: Build services section with midrange featured and pricing cards
description:
Replace the current "What We Build" section.

Requirements:
- Three tier cards in a grid
- **Middle card featured** (larger or highlighted) with "Most Popular" badge
- Tier 1: Managed Website — $1,000–$2,500
- Tier 2: Website + Lead System — $1,500–$4,500 (Most Popular)
- Tier 3: Website + Operations — $3,000–$10,000+
- Each card: title, price range, 3-4 bullet features, "Learn More" → /services
- Same section heading style as current page
- Use azimuth-ui Card, Text, Button, Stack components

Psychology: decoy effect (3 tiers), anchoring (price ranges).

title: Write hero section with problem-first copy and loss aversion framing
description:
Redesign the hero section of the landing page.

Requirements:
- Headline uses loss aversion: frame as problem/solution, not just feature list
  - Example: "Your website should be bringing in customers — not collecting dust."
- Subhead signals flexibility across industries: "Whether you run a law firm, a gym, or a plumbing business..."
- Two CTAs: primary "Get Started" (→ /contact), secondary "See How It Works" (→ /process)
- Keep existing layout, just replace copy and refine styling
- Use azimuth-ui components (Text, Button, Stack)
- Responsive, mobile-first

Psychology: loss aversion, authority, reciprocity (free consult implied).

title: Redesign landing page with psychology-driven copy and layout
description:
Full landing page redesign using sales psychology principles. Details in specs/landing-page.md.

Sections: Hero (problem-first framing), Services (midrange featured as Most Popular), Process, Portfolio, Pricing summary, Testimonials placeholder, Bottom CTA.

Tone: direct, warm, no jargon. Flexible across industries.
